subject: public office and religious tests
legal_effect: Bars a religious test as a qualification for federal office or public trust.
religion_connection: Expressly limits religious qualification by the federal government.
scope_note: Directly addresses federal office; state-office rules require separate analysis.
explanatory_authority: U.S. Constitution Annotated, Religious Test Clause materials
notes: Textual classification; not a law derived from religious doctrine.

subject: public-school prayer
legal_effect: Held unconstitutional official use of a state-composed prayer in public schools.
religion_connection: Limits government-sponsored religious exercise in public education.
scope_note: Does not itself prohibit private prayer or all private religious expression in public schools.
notes: Record later Establishment Clause cases separately.

subject: religious exercise and government burdens
legal_effect: Creates statutory protection against specified substantial governmental burdens on religious exercise through a compelling-interest and least-restrictive-means test.
religion_connection: The statute expressly protects religious exercise and was enacted after Employment Division v. Smith.
competing_causes: constitutional federalism and remedial-power limits shape present scope
scope_note: City of Boerne v. Flores limited RFRA’s application to state and local governments; federal applications remain central.
primary_authority: Religious Freedom Restoration Act of 1993, Pub. L. 103-141, 107 Stat. 1488; 42 U.S.C. §§ 2000bb–2000bb-4
explanatory_authority: RFRA findings and purposes; City of Boerne v. Flores, 521 U.S. 507 (1997)
notes: May also be indexed as a D-type government-burden limitation in a multi-label implementation.
